title: May December - "Insecure people are very dangerous, aren't they?"

commenti.body: Yeah and I’m not sure what to make of Elizabeth having sex with Joe. It definitely was irresponsible of her to do so but she doesn’t seem to reckon with it. I’m also not totally sure of her reason for doing so. Part of method acting? Some weird way of trying to “save” Joe? Or was it just sex with a vulnerable person because she wanted sex?

There is a really uncomfortable reading that Joe is sort a blank slate that these women are mapping themselves onto and that there is a seductive quality to his childlike naïveté. 

It also serves as a mirroring of Elizabeth in the stock room at the pet store. She has evolved from playing in the mind of Gracie to embodying her, or at least that’s what she’s trying to do. It’s arguable that she is just a bad actress and she has no idea what she’s doing.

Multiple interpretations as far as I can see.

For one, she is clearly trying to live inside Gracie as much as she can for the sake of the movie. She dresses like her, uses private material like the letter or the alleged diary entry that Gracie’s son tells her about to enhance her performance. That this also guides her towards having sex with her husband puts a finer point on how this movie is in part an indictment of the morality of art - if the path to making something ‘true’ involves potentially destroying a marriage, is it worth making?

An extension of this is that it makes it more plain that there are no heroes or villains in this story. Elizabeth is clearly dissatisfied with her relationship, and the fact that she is willing to be disloyal with zero arm-twisting shows that she is a damaged soul with a broken moral compass, just like Gracie.

The other commenter has said the last bit I was thinking of already re: Joe just kind of being a concept or a blank slate rather than a distinct human being. The scene cements that he’s that for both Gracie and Elizabeth, further insinuating that the two women are in fact more alike than they at first seem.

Yes, I agree with you! I thought that Elizabeth was delusional and almost as disturbing as Gracie.. I feel like both Elizabeth and Gracie became one, psychologically.. just in different ways.. 

IDK if the writers/filmmakers intended this, but to me it felt like Elizabeth was just slipping more and more into Gracie's mind and was herself, in some dark twisted way drawn into the Gracie-Joe taboo, intrigued by Joe himself, and was attracted to it all.. in some subconscious way.. It's not clearly shown, but this is what I got from her performance - and, it may not be the only facet of her psyche in being drawn to Gracie-Joe, but, could be one of the facets of her amusement.. It is especially clear starting in the scene where she lays on the steps of the storeroom/backroom of pet-shop and imagines/enacts their sexual act alone - there is a brief moment she gets into it and then smiles and snaps out of it, fleeting moments during her interactions with Joe, ofcourse sex with Joe, and her mindblowing enactment of Gracie's letter, and the last scene... It almost makes me feel like, she is somehow in a twisted way curiously enjoying the taboo in a safe way - in a way that is legal, in a way that she can vicariously delve into the dark forbidden twisted side of humanity.. 

I felt bad and yet so shocked at how Gracie is unaware and blind to it all.. and it makes sense too, only someone as unaware and delusional as herself could do such a thing and live with it.. I am not sure if she is capable of feeling insecure or secure.. this person is effed up on a very different scale. She's beyond psycho-analysis IMO.

Either way, both Gracie and Elizabeth were such disturbing characters I have ever seen on cinema.. and God, what writing, direction and acting.. so many layers .. such mindblowing script, direction and performances.. one could draw so many interpretations in so many scenes.. God I loved it. 

Joe was just heartbreaking.. he remained a child even at the age of 36, when his children were graduating, he was younger than them, still a trembling child at heart, but he's the most selfless person on this planet..

I don't get the, " I'm very secure scene ", Is she trying to say that the rape actually didn't happened from her brother and It actually didn't happen?, did she actually have a relationship with her son?, is it to shown that she is just a monster unforgivable?, all of this questions I have about that scene, what are they trying to say?, was she actually assaulted by her brothers?, was it a ploy with her son? Or she just supposed that her son talked to the actress about this, great movie overall
